text:
incident-bot: PagerDuty alert fired -> INC-2026-8457: service=redwood-inference-serving, symptom=GPU memory pressure / CUDA OOM spikes, cluster=us-west-2-gpu, severity=high. link: https://pagerduty.example/INC-2026-8457

pagerduty: Page: alex (primary oncall) — triggered 2m ago

alex: acked. on it. grabbing logs and nvidia-smi

sophia: seeing elevated 5xx on inference route /v1/chat and /v1/generate, p50 latency up 3x, error rate +18% over baseline :chart_with_upwards_trend:

maya: logs show repeated stack: `RuntimeError: CUDA out of memory. Tried to allocate 1.25 GiB (GPU 0; 31.75 GiB total capacity)` inside model-infer container

alex: ssh to gpu-12-3, running `nvidia-smi -q -d MEMORY` now

alex: paste: 
```\nGPU 0 Memory Usage
    Used                           : 31.4 GiB
    Total                          : 31.75 GiB
Processes:  python (PID 4521) model-infer --batch=8
```

sam: sounds like a sudden increase in batch concurrency. Any rollout recently?

lee: checked deploys — no production rollout in last 60m. autoscaler pushed more replicas 5m ago due to higher qps

carter: two paying customers reporting higher latency in status page: AcmeCorp, AtlasHealth. CS notified and opened tickets. Not yet a partial outage but user impact visible

maya: tailing container logs: repeated lines: `CUDA error: out of memory\nRuntimeError: CUDA out of memory. If reserved memory is >> allocated, try emptying cache.`

alex: temporary mitigation: reduce per-replica concurrency and reduce batch_size to 1 for hot model. Applying patch to config map `inference-throttle` to set model-infer.batch_size=1 and concurrency=1

ops-bot: Running config patch: `kubectl -n inference set env deployment/model-infer BATCH_SIZE=1 MAX_CONCURRENCY=1`

ops-bot: Scaling down model-infer replicas from 12 -> 8 to reduce aggregate memory pressure (reason: emergency mitigation)

alex: executing node-level action: `kubectl drain gpu-12-3 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --timeout=5m` to evacuate problematic workloads

lee: moving traffic to gpu-7 and gpu-9 pools via routing rule: `routing: prefer: [gpu-7,gpu-9]` in temp policy

sam: also enabling kv-cache eviction policy to aggressive-prune (reduces memory usage at cost of more compute) — pushed via rollout job

sophia: after config change metrics: 5xx down to baseline-ish, p95 latency trending down but still 20% above normal. CUDA OOMs dropped to near-zero on gpu-12-3 logs

alex: confirm GPU mem freed on gpu-12-3, rerunning `nvidia-smi` shows 3 GiB used. starting to uncordon after validations

maya: note: we saw a single container repeatedly reallocate big tensors in a loop — suspect bad prompt amplification in customer workload. Adding rate limit for that API key until postmortem

carter: customer comms: sent interim note to AcmeCorp & AtlasHealth — saying we mitigate and investigating root cause. CS asked for ETA: told them 2 hours for full stability and postmortem within 48 hours

alex: created incident ticket in PagerDuty and Ops board: INC-2026-8457, linked to runbook `gpu-cuda-oom`. Adding tags: gpu-pressure, high-priority, customer-impact

ops-bot: Reminder: collect `kubectl logs -p` from restarted pods, `dmesg | tail` on node, and `nvidia-smi --query` outputs. Archiving logs to S3 bucket s3://redwood-ops/incidents/INC-2026-8457

sam: proposed follow-ups: 1) limit batch_size per model by default, 2) add autoscaler hysteresis for GPU pools, 3) add kv-cache eviction thresholds per workload, 4) alert when single PID consumes >80% mem for >30s

lee: +1 on autoscaler hysteresis. Also recommend soft cap on burst concurrency for GPU-backed endpoints

maya: starting runbook steps for root cause analysis. grabbing heap/profile dumps from relevant containers now (may take ~15m)

alex: handoff: i'm going offline in 20m. handing to maya (secondary) — maya, you own incident until cleared. I'll post a handoff summary in #incidents.

maya: ack, taking over. current state: mitigations applied, user impact reduced but ongoing monitoring for 1 hr. will escalate if regressions.

carter: created incident update in #incidents with summary and list of affected customers. tagging legal/security for customer data review (no data exfil / only performance impact)

pagerduty: Incident INC-2026-8457 acknowledged by alex at 1826004340. Escalation paused. Next escalation window 30m.

alex: thanks team :pray: good run. maya — reach out if anything spikes.

maya: will compile timeline and collect artifacts. postmortem + action items due EOD +48h.

incident-bot: Incident thread closed in Slack (thread open for follow-up notes).
